title: The Hidden Life of Stars: Embedded Beginnings to Asymptotic Giant Branch Endings in the PHANGS─JWST Sample. I. Catalog of Mid-infrared Sources
question: Generate a multiwavelength catalog and classification framework of 10 and 21 um compact mid-infrared sources in 19 nearby PHANGS-JWST galaxies to study young stellar clusters and evolved dusty stars.

data.sensitivity: typical 1sigma noise ~6.2 mJy beam^-1 (~0.17 K) in 2.5 km s^-1 channels

what.value: CO(2-1) emission line maps and galaxy properties

evidence.quote: We used CO (2-1) emission line maps from the PHANGS–ALMA project (cite: Leroy2021).
Table [\[tab:galaxies\]](#tab:galaxies) lists the galaxies included in this study along with their properties, as reported in (cite: lee2023) and (cite: Leroy2021).
We further use the morphological masks of sub-galactic environments from (cite: Querejeta2021).

what.value: MUSE emission line maps and stellar continuum

evidence.quote: For this work, we use emission line maps from (cite: phangs-muse), which were generated using the MUSE Data Analysis Pipeline (DAP).
In particular, we rely on H$\alpha$ and H$\beta$ emission line maps that are corrected for the Milky Way Foreground extinction as well as the $E(B-V)$ reddening maps from (cite: Belfiore2023)

what.value: SAGE-LMC spectroscopic classifications and photometric catalogs of evolved stars

evidence.quote: We use the `PARSEC` stellar evolutionary tracks (section [4.1.2](#sec:parsec)) to classify RSGs, O-AGBs, and C-AGBs, which we validate with observations from the SAGE-LMC survey (cite: Jones2017; Jones2018).

By cross-matching our exposed sources with the “nebular” catalog from (cite: neb_catalog) using a maximum separation of 1$''$ (comparable to the typical MUSE PSF), we find that about 77% of the exposed clusters are associated with MUSE nebular regions across our sample of 19 galaxies.

recipe.goal: Convolve multiwavelength JWST and HST images to common catalog resolutions and subtract diffuse emission
recipe.method: Convolve maps to 0.36'' (F1130W) for the 10 um catalog and 0.67'' (F2100W) for the 21 um catalog using jwst_kernels, mask saturated galaxy centers in NGC 1365 and NGC 7496 using STPSF, and decompose F1000W and F2100W maps using Constrained Diffusion (CD)
key_parameters: Use scale 2 of CD decomposition for F2100W and sum of scales 1 and 2 for F1000W; central mask radius ~18'' for NGC 1365 and NGC 7496

recipe.goal: Identify compact 10 and 21 um sources and measure multiwavelength photometry and completeness limits
recipe.method: Run ASTRODENDRO on CD-filtered F1000W and F2100W maps, measure peak surface brightness on unfiltered convolved JWST/HST maps with annular background subtraction, sample native ALMA CO(2-1) and MUSE maps at source positions, and run artificial source tests (AST)
key_parameters: Dendrogram threshold = min + 5 * step; min_npix = 41 (F2100W) or 10 (F1000W); min_delta = 3 * step; min separation = 0.33'' (F1000W) or 0.17'' (F2100W); background annulus = 2x to 3x PSF size

recipe.goal: Classify sources and analyze correlations and luminosity functions
recipe.method: Classify sources into exposed/embedded young clusters, RSGs, O-AGBs, C-AGBs, CPNs, B[e], WRs, foreground stars, and background galaxies using flux ratio cuts from CIGALE, PARSEC/COLIBRI, and SAGE-LMC; fit Halpha-F2100W linear relation and Pareto-lognormal luminosity functions
key_parameters: Flux ratio cuts in Table 3; Gaia DR3 parallax_over_error > 3 within 2''; F200W semi-major/semi-minor axis ratio > 1.5 for background galaxies
assumptions: BC03 SSP with Z=0.02, Chabrier IMF, A_V = 1 and 10 mag, R_V = 3.1, q_PAH = 0.95 to 3.8%, U_min = 10, alpha = 2 for CIGALE cluster models; Kroupa IMF for PARSEC models

answer_key.quantity: Number of compact sources detected at 21 um (F2100W)

evidence.quote: We detect 24,945 compact sources at 21 $\mu$m and 55,581 at 10 $\mu$m.
We ran this algorithm on both the F1000W and F2100W bands across our targets and found 24945 sources in the F2100W maps and 55581 in the F1000W maps.

answer_key.quantity: Number of compact sources detected at 10 um (F1000W)

evidence.quote: We detect 24,945 compact sources at 21 $\mu$m and 55,581 at 10 $\mu$m.
We ran this algorithm on both the F1000W and F2100W bands across our targets and found 24945 sources in the F2100W maps and 55581 in the F1000W maps.

answer_key.quantity: Median 50% completeness limit for 10 um (F1000W) catalog

evidence.quote: The median detection limit at the F1000W resolution is 5 $\mu$Jy, while at F2100W, it is about five times higher at 24 $\mu$Jy.

The uncertainty in the completeness limit due to fitting error is less than 0.2 $\mu$Jy for the F1000W catalog and 0.7 $\mu$Jy for the F2100W catalog, as calculated from the covariance matrix of the curve fitting.

score_reason: All underlying survey data (PHANGS-JWST, PHANGS-HST, PHANGS-ALMA, PHANGS-MUSE) are public, the final catalogs are publicly archived with a DOI, and the custom analysis pipeline (Neloura) for source detection, photometry, and artificial star tests is publicly released on GitHub.
rediscovery_reason: Public high-level image mosaics and public analysis code allow full reproduction of the 10 and 21 um source catalogs, completeness limits, classifications, and luminosity function slopes.
